claims.text: Positive heat of mixing between refractory alloying elements and Cu makes the precursor prone to phase separation.
Advanced computational free-energy sampling can identify optimal reaction conditions that overcome the positive heat-of-mixing challenge.
Conditions identified by free-energy sampling can enable large-scale reaction synthesis of an RHEA/Cu composite.
The proposed reaction synthesis will produce a stable composite microstructure.
Metadynamics or kinetic Monte Carlo can determine optimal synthesis temperature, pressure, and reaction time.
The processing environment should use high-temperature conditions representative of nuclear-reactor applications.
The RHEA/Cu interfacial microstructure formed during reaction synthesis mediates the resulting composite structure.
Mapping the free-energy landscape at the RHEA/Cu interface can identify processing conditions that mitigate the thermodynamic penalty associated with positive heat of mixing.
Mitigating the thermodynamic penalty will make the reaction more homogeneous at large scale.
A more homogeneous large-scale reaction will reduce phase separation and stabilize the microstructure.
The synthesized composite will have a refined microstructure.
The synthesized composite will exhibit less phase separation and greater homogeneity than a conventionally processed composite.
Conventional mixing and rapid high-temperature sintering tend to produce phase separation in refractory-element/Cu composites.
The effectiveness of the method depends on the accuracy of its free-energy-landscape predictions.
Failure to capture kinetic factors or impurities may limit the method's applicability.
Translation of computationally optimized conditions into practical synthesis remains uncertain because of kinetic limitations and experimental variability.
